content:
Noah: From today's presales call  customer requires primary compute in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), deterministic failover to Montreal (ca-central-1). Control plane cannot transit US. BYOK via customer HSM mandatory. Any immediate red flags?
Lilly: Hosted control plane is US by default so that's a blocker. Options: Private control-plane in customer VPC (fast) or Dedicated with regional control-plane (contract). For POC recommend Private.
Ankit: Data path wise we can tenant-pin to eu-central-1 with failover to ca-central-1. We support customer-managed keys in both regions. Need to confirm provider mapping (AWS v GCP) for each region.
Jules: Compliance: will produce subprocessor register but note AWS staff in DE and GCP staff in CA are subprocessors. Need to confirm that no telemetry or support tooling leaks to US.
Noah: Customer says keys live in their cloud account (they run HSM in ca-central-1). Good?
Ankit: Yes  customer-managed HSM removes a lot of legal friction. We'll still need KMS grants + IAM runbook + peering. Estimate 30-45 eng hours for POC setup.
Lilly: Pricing: propose two lines - (A) 30d POC: setup fee + small reserved units + egress buffer for failover tests; (B) Production Private/Dedicated: monthly commit + BYOK integration + optional SLA uplift. Include egress estimate for DE<->CA replication.
ComplianceBot: Added note: attach SOC2 + ISO artifacts and include SOW clause: "control plane deployed in customer VPC; telemetry exports disabled unless explicitly authorized."
Noah: I'll draft routing sample and SOW language and send to buyer. @Lilly @Ankit please add pricing numbers. Schedule ops sync tomorrow. 
Lilly: Will do. Short shadowtest during POC to capture flow logs and prove no US transit.
